$comment: The security scanning settings, every key at its built-in default. Copy this file to your repository's root as security-settings.json and change what you need; a missing file means these defaults. Every key has an environment twin that wins over the file: SECURITY_ENABLED, SECURITY_SEVERITY, SECURITY_FAIL_ON, SECURITY_<JOB> for each job's switch, SECURITY_<JOB>_<KEY> for its options (androidPermissions -> SECURITY_BINARIES_ANDROID_PERMISSIONS) and SECURITY_LLM_<KEY> for the llm block. An invalid value fails the run.

code.$rules: The repository's own Semgrep rule files or directories, added to the community TypeScript, secrets and OWASP packs. Each path must exist.

bundle.$hosts: Hosts the exported bundle may name over https. Empty turns the check off; once listed, any other host is a low-severity note, so a new third-party endpoint is seen in review.
bundle.$cleartextHosts: Hosts an http:// URL in the bundle may name without a finding (MASTG-TEST-0233/0321). Add a host only with the reason it is never fetched by the shipped app.

binaries.$androidPermissions: Dangerous Android permissions the app is allowed to request (MASTG-TEST-0254), e.g. android.permission.CAMERA.
binaries.$exportedComponents: Exported activities, services and receivers allowed without a permission (MASTG-TEST-0364..0366), by class name.
binaries.$atsExceptionDomains: Domains allowed an App Transport Security exception for insecure HTTP (MASTG-TEST-0322).

review.$comment: Off by default: it sends the diff to the configured LLM provider. Needs llm.provider, llm.model and the provider's API key.

review-codebase.$comment: Off by default: it sends the codebase to the configured LLM provider and costs minutes and tokens. Runs on the release pull request only.

llm.$comment: Shared by review and review-codebase. provider is openai (any OpenAI-compatible endpoint through OPENAI_BASE_URL) or anthropic; effort is none (a model with no reasoning switch), low, medium, high or max.
